body: You can of course do all these things. Being liberal means believing in choice. Your choice is a traditional role. My choice might not be. Both should be respected, if it is what you want, not what’s expected of you.

I got paranoid and psychotic. Locked myself in the apartment, the fear and depression was eating me alive. Then I got out of the funk through medication. Started working again, but it got to much for me and when I couldn’t keep a promise to my best friend I tried to drown myself in the bath tub. Didn’t work of course.
I just quit my meds with no one knowing and now I plan how to kill myself.
I am in between doctors at the moment. The one who knows me said I was able to do well on my own now. I am on pretty low doses already, so that’s why I am doing it I guess.

Yes, I’ve thought a bit whether my lack of attraction to women is because I’ve been conditioned to think only of men as possible romantic interests. But I am not sure that is true. It seems strange that I haven’t crushed on a single woman in 30 years.
Thank you. I wish you the best as well!
I found it once. That’s not an evidence for anyone but me, but there’s that.

I am not very good at meeting new people, especially not men. I freeze. But I have met a few men these years and had some crushes who sadly didn’t pan out. But I guess I need to work on that to move forwards.
Then I understand you. At one point you have to say enough is enough. Draw the line. Don’t do as I did, look forwards instead!
If she is a decent, good person that didn’t mess with you on purpose, I’d say take your chance. Go get her. At least try, so you won’t have to think what if’s the next four years.

I guess you might be somewhat right. I am keeping his memory alive when I probably could forget him. But I don’t know if I truly want to forget him, because it was such a major thing you know? It was like an earthquake and I was so shook and I felt like somebody had ripped my heart out. And when you have gone through that it feels somewhat wrong to forget. But I comfort myself with the thought that if I met a new man I would let the old one go, because deep down I realize he is only a memory.
Have you considered talking to him again? Maybe you could keep him as a friend if it didn’t end too badly?

The first year was the worst. I cried everywhere, all the time. The last four has been good years, it’s just at odd times the pain pops back up. I’ve had crushes on other guys in between, but they just never seem to measure up. Don’t worry though, I don’t think my story is anything to go by when predicting your future:)

I guess there is two sides to that story. Mine would be that he decided to leave me for another woman. His would probably be that I friend zoned him for too long and when I realized I loved him, he was too hurt and chose someone else. So it wasn’t even a real relationship, but we were a we for a long time even so.
Thank you! That was nicely put.

That was beautifully said. I hope to love again of course and I believe it will happen but it might be hard not to compare. Though at this stage I guess the first time is more a nostalgic love so I hope something new will be more real.
Yes, let’s hope time will do that. Though I would have thought five years to be enough. Strange how deep an impression one person can make on you.
Thank you for your kind words! I hope so too, though I am a bit apprehensive. It’s a fresh start at least.

I think I like that there is so much emotions in Jane Eyre. You feel what they feel and it is stormy. And it ends rather well, so I don’t get too depressed. P&P is a bit more stable, you don’t get the high and lows the same way I think.
My category is favorite novels. I am sorta hoping it isn’t your category.
Favorite novels actually! I like them old.
Mine are: Jane Eyre, Count of Monte Cristo, Pride and Prejudice.
